newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gas regulator slashes tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gas regulator slashes tariffs.

text.p: Argentina's gas industry regulator Enargas said Friday it was cutting tariffs for distribution and transport companies by 4.5-6.5 percent for five years from January 1998.

"These reductions of about $400 million will benefit the consumer via tariff cuts of about 4.5-4.8 percent for the distribution companies and 5.2-6.5 percent for transport companies," Enargas said in a news release.
The regulator said this is the first tariff revision since the privatization of the state gas company which divided the industry up into eight distribution companies and two transport companies.
The tariff revision process began in 1995 and suppliers and consumers put forward their arguments at a public hearing at the end of May this year.

"The new margins take into account efficiency improvements that the regulator believes the license holders can attain in the next five years," said Enargas, adding that the main beneficiaries would be small consumers since big industrial clients already receive major discounts.
The regulator listed the following tariff reductions, by company, to be applied in one go on January 1, 1998:
Transportadora de Gas del Sur 6.5 pct
Transportadora de Gas del Norte 5.2 pct
Distribuidora de Gas del Centro 4.7 pct
